screens_reviewed: Single screenshot (iphone/light/20-settings.png) covering the full Settings route: header, Appearance (Theme), Text & reading (Text size + Dyslexia-friendly font), Account, and the Sign out CTA.
verdict: A clean, well-structured settings screen that correctly uses the shared ScaledText/ScaledParagraph primitives, the responsive content container, and design-system color/radius tokens. Layout, hierarchy, and tap targets read well on iPhone. The main concern is a likely double top-inset (the root Stack adds a fixed paddingTop of 20 on top of the header's own insets.top), and a screen full of hardcoded numeric font sizes/dimensions rather than tokens.

improvements.suggestion: The root navigator already applies a fixed contentStyle paddingTop of 20 to every Stack screen (app/_layout.tsx:1376-1379), and Settings is registered as a Stack.Screen with headerShown false (app/_layout.tsx:1389). The header here then adds insets.top again, so the safe-area gap is effectively 20 + insets.top. In the screenshot the title sits comfortably clear of the Dynamic Island, so it is not broken, but the stacking is fragile across devices. Consider letting the screen own its safe area (e.g. drop the fixed paddingTop 20 for this route, or have the header use only insets.top) so the inset is applied once.

improvements.location: app/settings.tsx (e.g. fontSize 22 line 105, 15 line 349, 13 line 358, 12 line 305; height 72 line 130, height 64 line 181, paddingBottom 12 line 82)
improvements.suggestion: Sizes and box dimensions are raw numbers rather than $size/$space tokens from tamagui.config.ts. This is consistent with the codebase's prevailing pattern (the design-system spacing object only exposes screenPaddingHorizontal/Vertical, and ScaledText is built to scale raw numeric fontSize), so it is not a defect, but centralizing the type ramp (e.g. section title 12, row label 15, header 22) into named tokens would make the scale easier to keep consistent across screens.

improvements.location: app/settings.tsx Dyslexia-friendly font row (React Native Switch, lines 228-234)
improvements.suggestion: The toggle uses the bare react-native Switch rather than a shared design-system primitive, with trackColor/thumbColor wired from tokens inline. It renders correctly here, but since the rest of the screen routes styling through the design system, a thin shared Switch wrapper would keep track/thumb colors consistent if tokens change.
improvements.evidence: app/settings.tsx:10,228-234; image shows iOS-style toggle in off state

tamagui_notes: design_system_components_used (ScaledParagraph, ScaledText) is honored: every text node uses ScaledText for labels/headings and ScaledParagraph for body copy (app/settings.tsx:102,149,245,302,346,354,385,392), so the auditor text-size preference will scale this screen correctly (ScaledText.tsx:2295-2321 in core.md).

Color and radius usage is token-driven via useDesignSystem: colors.surface, colors.border, colors.primary/primarySoft, radii.button/lg, colors.danger/dangerSoft (app/settings.tsx:85,131-134,259-262), matching lib/design-system.ts.

Horizontal padding and the scroll content container come from the responsive system (layout.screenPaddingHorizontal line 79; getResponsiveContentContainerStyle lines 112-115), so the screen centers and gutters correctly on wider canvases.
platform_notes: Safe-area top: handled (insets.top on the header, app/settings.tsx:81) plus the root Stack's fixed paddingTop 20; title clears the Dynamic Island in the screenshot. See double-top-inset improvement for the stacking concern.
Safe-area bottom: scroll content adds insets.bottom + 32 bottom padding (app/settings.tsx:113), so the Sign out CTA and last section clear the home indicator.
Thumb reach: the primary destructive CTA (Sign out, height 52, full width) sits at the bottom of the scroll within easy thumb reach (app/settings.tsx:257-279).

Tap targets: back button is 40x40 (app/settings.tsx:89-90) — below the 44pt iOS guideline but visually fine and not a hard failure; theme/text-size option buttons (72/64 tall, flex 1) are comfortably large.
not_assessable: Exact WCAG contrast of danger (#B5483D) Sign out text on dangerSoft over white surface — estimated near AA for 15px bold but not measured.
Runtime behavior of theme/text-size/dyslexic-font toggles (only the light + Default + off state is captured).
How the header inset renders on non-notch / smaller iPhones vs this Dynamic Island device.
score_rationale: Solid and ships with minor polish: correct use of shared scaled-text primitives, token-driven colors/radii, responsive container, and good safe-area/thumb-reach handling. Held back from 9-10 by the likely double top-inset stacking (fixed 20 + insets.top) and pervasive hardcoded sizes/dimensions; no critical defects observed.
